issue_context.title: [Coverity CID: 236647] Unchecked return value in drivers/sensor/bmp388/bmp388_trigger.c
issue_context.body:
Static code scan issues found in file:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/8c68a7a587b884fb12ee6a31658281b2f9929485/drivers/sensor/bmp388/bmp388_trigger.c#L157

Category: Error handling issues
Function: `bmp388_trigger_mode_init`
Component: Drivers
CID: [236647](https://scan9.coverity.com/reports.htm#v29726/p12996/mergedDefectId=236647)


Details:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/8c68a7a587b884fb12ee6a31658281b2f9929485/drivers/sensor/bmp388/bmp388_trigger.c#L157

```
151                    cfg->gpio_int.pin,
152                    GPIO_INPUT | cfg->gpio_int.dt_flags);
153    
154         gpio_init_callback(&data->gpio_cb,
155                    bmp388_gpio_callback,
156                    BIT(cfg->gpio_int.pin));
>>>     CID 236647:  Error handling issues  (CHECKED_RETURN)
>>>     Calling "gpio_add_callback" without checking return value (as is done elsewhere 37 out of 45 times).
157         gpio_add_callback(cfg->gpio_int.port, &data->gpio_cb);
158         gpio_pin_interrupt_configure(cfg->gpio_int.port,
159                          cfg->gpio_int.pin,
160                          GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE);
161    
162         return 0;
7 new defect(s) introduced to Zephyr found with Coverity Scan.
11 defect(s), reported by Coverity Scan earlier, were marked fixed in the recent build analyzed by Coverity Scan.
```

For more information about the violation, check the [Coverity Reference](https://scan9.coverity.com/doc/en/cov_checker_ref.html#static_checker_CHECKED_RETURN). ([CWE-252](http://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/252.html))

Please fix or provide comments in coverity using the link:

https://scan9.coverity.com/reports.htm#v29271/p12996

Note: This issue was created automatically. Priority was set based on classification
of the file affected and the impact field in coverity. Assignees were set using the CODEOWNERS file.

review_comments: gpio_add_callback() returns 0 if successful, positive is not specified at all, therefore original `if (rc != 0)`  is more correct.

Checking for `rc < 0` is correct according to function documentation, since we want to evaluate for a failure:

` * @return 0 if successful, negative errno code on failure.`
Again, positive is not specified at all, you change it so that it does not handle unspecified return value, that is not right.

Checking for positive values is, strictly speaking, undefined behavior since the function does not mention such case. Let's say one day `gpio_add_callback` returns a positive number to indicate a count, uid, etc. The code that uses `rc < 0` will still do the right job, i.e. return in case of error. The code using `rc != 0` will return even if there is no error.
Adding 0.5 and casting to int is usually a sign of trying to round to the nearest integer. Why was it removed?

I'm not sure what was the intention, but the expression without the `+ 0.5` is equivalent. I checked the [datasheet](https://www.sensirion.com/fileadmin/user_upload/customers/sensirion/Dokumente/9_Gas_Sensors/Sensirion_Gas_Sensors_SGP40_Datasheet.pdf) (Table 9) and this rounding is not mentioned, this is why I ended up removing it.

> the expression without the `+ 0.5` is equivalent.

Adding 0.5 and casting to `int` rounds to the nearest integer. Integer division truncates down.

> (Table 9)

I just looked at the datasheet and I think this is a typo; you mean table 10, right?

> this rounding is not mentioned, this is why I ended up removing it.

The formula in table 10 looks like an abstract mathematical equation for converting a percentage from 0 to 100 to ticks from 0 to 65,535, where footnote 4 on page 3 says that ticks are proportional to the log of the resistance of the sensing layer. So this sure looks like an attempt to get the nearest integer to something that varies continuously.

Why not use the usual idiom for rounding to the nearest integer that stays in integers without requiring floating point?

> @gmarull
> I was not able to review your changes earlier. I see in that line can happen potential overflow. Variable `tmp` can have maximum value 130. That means equation `(tmp * 65535) / 100` result 85195 will be definitely bigger than `int16_t` of the `t_ticks` variable.
> 
> `t_ticks` is `int16_t`. Maximum is `#define __INT16_MAX__ 0x7fff` or `32767`

The function domain goes in both cases (temp and humidity) from `[0, 65535]`, which is the range if `uint16_t`. So in fact, the variables storing ticks should be `uint16_t` type. See #38058
@leonardp You're probably the person who has the full context, so feel free to open a PR with your preferred solution.

> `rh_ticks1 = (int16_t)((float)(tmp * 0xFFFF / 100U) + 0.5);` would do what you mean I guess

Ah yes, you are right, sorry for missing that. It seems like we are on the same page about applying the usual `(numerator + (denominator / 2)) / denominator` idiom; will wait for a PR from @leonardp .
see: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/38075
Is it clearer to use `UINT16_MAX`?
I thought about changing to `UINT16_MAX`, but as datasheet uses 65535 number in their formulae I thought it would be easier to understand what's going on.
